name: Nantong
title: Nantong Ship Gauging: UTM on the Yangtze and at Yangkou
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Nantong for bulk carriers, product and chemical tankers and LNG carriers: holds, ballast tanks, decks and piping gauged.
h1: Thickness Measurement for Ships at Nantong's River Berths, Repair Yards and Yangkou Port
intro: Nantong lies on the north bank of the Yangtze, upstream of Shanghai, and its berths run from riverside bulk and chemical terminals to the deep-water coastal port at Yangkou. Bulk carriers, product and chemical tankers, LNG carriers and river-sea coasters call here, and yards on this reach of the river take ships in for repair. A Nantong job usually means a ship tied up long enough for holds, tanks or piping to be opened. For each one, a technician team flies out from India and joins the vessel through its agent.

highlights.h: River berths that hold ships for days
highlights.p: Bulk carriers discharging coal, ore or grain at Langshan and the other river port areas, and tankers working the chemical jetties at Rugao and Jianghai, often stay alongside for several days, which is enough time to open swept holds and certified ballast tanks for measurement.

highlights.h: Repair yards on the same reach
highlights.p: Nantong and Jiangyin, on the opposite bank, both have yards that dock and repair ocean-going ships. Readings taken at a Nantong cargo berth can become the pre-docking steel estimate for a yard a short distance away, with the same measurement grid carried into the dock.

highlights.h: Yangkou, a coastal port for gas and chemicals
highlights.p: At Rudong on the Yellow Sea coast, Yangkou receives LNG carriers for CNPC's import terminal, chemical tankers and heavy-lift ships. Gauging there is confined to deck structure, accommodation and machinery-space piping, and it is planned within strict terminal permit rules.

port.h: Nantong: a river port, a shipbuilding district and a coastal gateway
p: Nantong occupies the north bank of the Yangtze where the river begins to widen into its estuary, facing the Suzhou riverside ports across the water and linked to them by the Sutong cable-stayed bridge. Ocean-going ships reach the city's river terminals through the estuary channels past Shanghai, under pilotage and the river's vessel traffic management, and the deep-water channel dredged on the lower Yangtze lets sizeable bulk carriers and tankers come this far upstream. The river is tidal here and the current is strong, and visibility can drop sharply in the fog that settles on the lower Yangtze in winter and spring. Berthing, anchoring and any launch work are therefore planned around river conditions as much as around the cargo programme, and ships waiting for a berth or a pilot lie in designated river anchorages.

The port is divided into a string of river port areas and a group of coastal ones. On the river, Rugao and Jianghai handle oil products, liquid chemicals and petrochemicals, Tiansheng serves power stations, and Langshan takes bulk cargo, containers and break-bulk. The traffic this generates is varied: bulk carriers bringing coal and ore for riverside power stations and industry, MR product and chemical tankers, small container feeders, and the river-sea coasters that shuttle cargo between Yangtze ports and the coast. Many of the coastal ships are Chinese-flagged and classed locally, while bulk carriers and tankers arriving from abroad carry flags and classes from across the world, so a single visit to Nantong can involve thickness reports laid out on the formats of two or three different societies.

Nantong is also one of China's shipbuilding districts. The Rengang area on the river serves the COSCO yards, including the COSCO-Kawasaki joint venture that builds large container ships and bulk carriers, and COSCO has long run a ship-repair yard in the city with floating docks for ocean-going tonnage. Downstream, Qidong and Haimen, both inside Nantong's boundaries, host offshore and newbuilding yards. On the open Yellow Sea coast to the north-east, the port has been adding deep-water capacity: Yangkou, at Rudong, was built out over former tidal flats into a port with berths for ships of more than 50,000 tonnes, an LNG import terminal and a zone for liquid chemicals, while Lüsi, further along the same coast, forms another coastal port area.

facilities.h: Where a ship can be gauged around Nantong
p: At the river terminals, gauging fits around cargo work. A bulk carrier discharging at Langshan frees its holds one at a time, which suits tank top, hopper and frame readings as each hold is swept, while ballast tanks can be opened once the ship's trim and ballast plan allow it. Tankers at the Rugao and Jianghai chemical jetties offer deck plating, deck piping and ballast spaces, but cargo tanks only after the ship holds a gas-free certificate and the terminal agrees. Ships waiting at the river anchorages can be boarded by launch when current and visibility allow, which is not every day in the fog season.

For a full docking, ships go to the repair yards on this stretch of the Yangtze: COSCO's repair yard in Nantong, and CSSC Chengxi across the river at Jiangyin, which concentrates on repair and conversion and uses floating docks for bulk carriers and tankers. Yard work brings staging, lighting and cleaned spaces, so it is where survey gauging and re-gauging of renewed plating normally happen. At Yangkou the setting changes again: LNG carriers and chemical tankers at the coastal jetties can only have accessible structure and piping measured, under the terminal's hazardous-area rules and with instruments the terminal has accepted.
list: Langshan bulk and container berths — hold, hatch cover and ballast tank gauging on bulk carriers as discharge frees each space.
Rugao and Jianghai liquid berths — deck plating, deck piping and ballast spaces on product and chemical tankers, with cargo tanks only once gas-free certified.
River anchorages off Nantong — ballast-condition gauging by launch for buyers or before a docking, subject to current and visibility.
COSCO repair yard in Nantong — renewal and docking survey gauging with the ship in a floating dock or at the repair quay.
CSSC Chengxi at Jiangyin, across the river — repair and conversion dockings where readings from a Nantong berth carry over into the yard.
Yangkou port at Rudong — LNG carriers and chemical tankers; deck and machinery-space piping gauging within terminal rules.

context.h: Port state control, river rules and the Nantong trade
p: Foreign ships at Nantong are inspected by the China Maritime Safety Administration under the Tokyo MoU, and the Jiangsu branch of the MSA also oversees navigation on this crowded reach of the river. Because the Yangtze below Nanjing carries river-sea ships, coasters and ocean-going tonnage in the same channels, the authorities pay close attention to hull condition, steering gear and safety equipment, and a ship with obvious wastage at deck edges or holed ventilators invites questions at the gangway. China applies tighter emission rules on its inland waterways than at sea, including restrictions on discharging open-loop scrubber wash-water on the river, so scrubber-fitted ships coming upriver normally run closed-loop or change fuel and leave the system idle; operators should confirm the current rules before arrival.

Two commercial patterns add to the demand. Many river-sea and coastal ships trading to Nantong are older Chinese-flagged ships, and their owners use gauging to decide whether a ship still justifies another docking. Ocean-going bulk carriers and tankers, meanwhile, often reach Nantong at the end of a long laden voyage, which makes the post-discharge days a natural moment for a pre-docking estimate before a yard on the lower Yangtze or at Zhoushan. Ships built in the Nantong yards also come back to the region for warranty-period work and their first renewal survey, which gives owners the chance to compare early corrosion with the newbuilding plate thicknesses.

jobs.h: Gauging jobs we see at Nantong
jobs.p: Work at Nantong falls between the river berths, where ships stay for days but cargo comes first, and the yards, where the ship is opened up for survey. Most enquiries come from superintendents who want readings taken during a discharge so that the steel list is ready before the ship goes to dock, or from buyers inspecting a ship that happens to be in the river. Tanker and gas carrier scopes are narrower and depend on what each terminal permits. Every programme is checked against the ship's previous thickness report, and it is fixed once the berth window or dock date is firm.
list: Hold, hopper and inner bottom gauging on a bulk carrier discharging coal at a Nantong river berth, measured as each hold is swept, ahead of its third renewal survey.
Pre-docking steel estimate on a Handysize bulk carrier at a river anchorage before it shifts to a repair yard at Nantong or Jiangyin.
Deck, deck piping and ballast tank gauging on an MR chemical tanker at a Rugao jetty, in preparation for a CAP survey.
Renewal survey gauging and re-gauging of renewed plating on a bulk carrier in a floating dock at a Nantong repair yard.
Owner's condition gauging of an ageing river-sea coaster, to decide whether the steel needed at its next docking is worth spending.
Wash-water and overboard piping checks on a scrubber-fitted bulk carrier while its system is shut down on the river.

logistics: Shanghai Pudong and Hongqiao are the usual arrival airports, and Nantong Xingdong International Airport handles domestic and some regional flights; from Shanghai the team crosses to Nantong by road over the Sutong Bridge. Terminal passes, yard gate passes and any launch to a river anchorage are arranged through the ship's agent. Technicians travel from India on Chinese business visas supported by an invitation letter from a company in China, and port access paperwork for foreign personnel may also be needed, so the application starts as soon as a berth or dock date is known.
vessels: Ships in for repair or conversion

faqs.q: Can a bulk carrier be gauged while it discharges at a Nantong river berth?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is often the best window. Holds are measured as each one is emptied and swept, starting with the tank top, hopper plating and lower frames where wear from grabs and cargo is greatest. Ballast tanks are added when the ship's ballast plan lets them be emptied, ventilated and certified safe. We agree the order with the chief officer before arrival so the work follows the discharge rather than delaying it.

faqs.q: Does fog on the Yangtze affect anchorage work at Nantong?
faqs.a: It can. In the winter and spring months, dense fog on the lower Yangtze can stop launches and delay pilotage, and the strong tidal current makes boarding a ship at a river anchorage harder than at a sheltered sea anchorage. We therefore treat anchorage gauging at Nantong as weather-dependent, keep a priority list of spaces, and move whatever remains to the berth or the yard if conditions close in.

faqs.q: Is there a dock near Nantong for steel renewal?
faqs.a: Yes. Ship-repair yards work on this part of the river, in Nantong itself and at Jiangyin on the opposite bank, and the large repair centre at Zhoushan is further south. A pre-docking estimate made at a Nantong berth can therefore go straight to a yard close by, and the same measurement locations can be used in dock so the class surveyor sees one continuous record.

faqs.q: What can be measured on an LNG carrier at Yangkou?
faqs.a: Only what the terminal and the ship's permit system allow. Cargo containment is not entered at a discharge terminal, so the work concentrates on machinery-space, sea-water and ballast piping, deck structure away from hazardous zones and accessible ballast tanks. Instruments have to be accepted for the zone they are used in, and the programme is agreed with the terminal and the master before the team boards.

faqs.q: Can one trip cover ships at Nantong and Shanghai?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Nantong is a road journey from Shanghai, so a mobilisation can cover a ship at a Shanghai terminal or estuary anchorage and another at a Nantong berth or yard, provided the windows fall close together. Tell us both schedules early and we will build one visa application and one travel plan around them.
